extracted.intended_audience: reporters, journalists, content creators, and communicators who cover disability issues or people with disabilities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for journalists and content creators to expand and improve coverage of disability issues and people with disabilities, focusing on language, interviewing practices, and ethical newsroom principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic principles: accuracy, fairness and diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCDJ does not advocate a particular point of view; it is concerned with the journalistic principles of accuracy, fairness and diversity in news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize accuracy, fairness and diversity when reporting on disability; the center exists to support these journalistic principles and to help reporters expand and improve coverage of disability issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability Language Style Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive Disability Language Style Guide with recommendations about language and disability-related terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the NCDJ style guide's recommended language and terminology when writing about people with disabilities to avoid misrepresentation and stigmatizing language; the guide is offered as a primary resource for reporters and content creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for interviewing people with disabilities (tip sheets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tip sheets with best practices for interviewing people with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the center's interview best-practice guidance (available as tip sheets) to conduct respectful, accurate, and effective interviews with people who have disabilities; these resources are aimed at improving the quality of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and customized workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: The center offers training and resources that include ... customized workshops for individuals and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and news organizations are encouraged to use the center's trainings and workshops to build capacity and improve disability coverage practices in their newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve as a resource for reporters covering disability beats
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters who cover disability issues as a beat and those who may report on people with disabilities or disability issues may find the center a useful resource for information and the exchange of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The center promotes exchange of information and ideas among practitioners — implying that continual learning, consultation of authoritative resources, and peer exchange are part of producing high-quality disability coverage.
